short.hook: A monumental marble-lined Roman pool was found 7 meters underground.
script: A monumental marble-lined Roman pool was found 7 meters underground.
It's lined with over eight types of marble and has a preserved hypocaust heating system beneath.
The hypocaust circulates hot air through voids, heating the floor and pool water.
The pool is connected to a city cistern, showing advanced water and heating infrastructure.
Artifacts include a 5th century BC silver coin and a blue marble votive inscription.
The city’s name is debated—could it be Idomene or Dober?
Could the necropolis have been repurposed for military use later on?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A monumental marble-lined Roman pool was found 7 meters underground at Isar–Marvinci in North Macedonia. It features over eight types of marble and a well-preserved hypocaust heating system. Researchers note the pool is connected to a cistern, indicating advanced urban infrastructure. A silver coin from 500–480 BC and a blue marble inscription were also uncovered. The site's exact name remains uncertain—possibly Idomene or Dober—based on ancient sources. Source: Arkeonews, https://arkeonews.net/monumental-marble-lined-roman-pool-found-7-meters-underground/
Full case file: https://youtu.be/X8newfre5Ds
Images: Ad Meskens / CC BY-SA 3.0 / Wikimedia Commons; George E. Koronaios / CC0 / Wikimedia Commons
Some visuals are AI illustrations.
